note: States that resolution can generate continuous effects; sub-rules carry outcomes.

outcome: A continuous effect from a resolved spell or ability lasts for its stated duration, or until the end of the game if none is stated.
A for-as-long-as effect whose duration never starts or ends before it would first apply does nothing.
A resolved effect that modifies characteristics or control affects a fixed set of objects determined at resolution, while rules-modifying parts also affect later objects.
A variable such as X in a continuous effect is evaluated once on resolution.
An is-or-has characteristic effect applies as the permanent enters, so enter triggers see it, while becomes or gains applies afterwards.
A next-spell effect begins applying when the player next puts an appropriate spell on the stack and applies to that spell.

note: States that static abilities generate continuous effects.

outcome: A static ability effect applies at each moment to whatever its text indicates, so objects gaining or losing the property gain or lose the effect.
A static ability effect applies exactly while its source is on the battlefield or in the appropriate zone.
Static characteristic changes apply as a permanent enters, so it enters with modified values before enter triggers are checked.
A battlefield-only ability granted along with permission to play lasts as long as the permission effect states, or until game end.
